newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong new chief Tung formally declares wealth.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong new chief Tung formally declares wealth.

text.p: Hong Kong's post-colonial leader, Tung Chee-hwa, a rich former shipping magnate, has formally declared his financial assets in taking over China's new Special Administrative region.
Shanghai-born Tung, 60, made a statement of his wealth to the Chief Justice of the Court of Final Appeal, Andrew Li, on Tuesday to comply with transparency rules affecting officials.
The declaration by the new Chief Executive was put on record in compliance with new laws, but not publicly disclosed, a spokesman said on Wednesday.
Tung took office on Tuesday as Chief Executive when Hong Kong reverted to China after 156 years of British rule. The ex-colony is now the called the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

The spokesman gave no details of the assets. But Tung said last April he had a US$47.5 million stake in his family shipping firm, Orient Overseas (International) Ltd, based on market prices at that time.
The figure was based on his ownership of 80,835,548 non-voting shares, representing 15.6 percent of shipping group Orient Oversas (International) Ltd.
Tung also said in April that he owned nothing more than the stake in his family business, not even property.
His wife Betty was sole beneficial shareholder of a company which owns their two apartments in Hong Kong.
His villa in the prestige Deep Water Bay district of Hong Kong belonged to his family trust.
His April declaration said there were three apartments in the United States -- in New York, San Francisco and Salt Lake City -- which were owned by a trust benefiting his children.
